newsitem.title: UK: NNPC says no revision of March crude contract price.
newsitem.headline: NNPC says no revision of March crude contract price.

text.p: State Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) will not revise March term crude price formulas despite the heavy losses customers are likely to incur from a fall in spot market values, a senior NNPC official said on Friday.
"The honourable (oil) minister has reviewed the market situation this week and has directed that prices remain unchanged," the NNPC official said.
Spot Nigerian crude prices have fallen heavily in the past two weeks, leaving customers facing big losses versus the contract prices set by NNPC at the end of February for March loadings.
"The market is giving us cause for concern. But we can't change prices because customers are hurting in one month," said the NNPC official. "We have to take a longer term perspective."

Forcados, one of Nigeria's two biggest export streams, on Friday was being priced on spot markets for March lifting at parity with benchmark Dated Brent. NNPC priced the grade for March at Brent plus 47 cents.
Bonny Light, valued at Dated Brent plus 40 cents on the spot market, was undercutting contract prices by 18 cents a barrel.
The NNPC official said he expected Nigerian oil lifters to return average profits this year of at least as much as in 1996.
NNPC aimed to allow a margin for profits and business costs of at least 11 cents a barrel, he said.
The official said he expected customers to honour contracts despite the prospect of losses.
"By and large our customers have supported us in a difficult market but there are a few lagging behind," he said. "People who have signed contracts should lift."
Nigeria sells some 850,000 bpd of crude through contracts with traders and refiners, adjusting prices every month according to NNPC's assesment of the spot market.
